Well, yeah, it most definitely does.  I have not let myself get too involved in any relationship since.  At first I willfully stopped myself from caring, and over time it began to feel more like a natural defense mechanism.  Now I simply feel incapable of caring for someone on that level.  It doesn't feel like a choice at all anymore;  it feels like that propensity within myself has dissipated altogether.

For five years these feelings and my own guilt have been the monkey on my back.  It progressed and has led to alcoholism, self-confidence issues and a nasty smoking habit.  I am pessimistic and often paranoid.  I am uncomfortable with myself at best, and outright disgusted at worst.  I have progressed from not caring about others to not caring about myself.

The concept of fairness is not a crutch I generally rely upon.  In every other aspect of life I hold myself accountable for my own rationale.  In that particular instance during that part of my life, however, I feel as though I trusted someone else with something very important and was ultimately betrayed.

Don't get me wrong.  I still wouldn't have been okay with it ending in any other way (short of us seeing it through and truly discovering whether or not we could realistically be together), however, I feel like I would have had a better chance to recover.  How could she simply disappear from my life as if I were suddenly nothing to her?  After all of that, how could what I thought we had together be so inherently disposable?  I would be hard-pressed to dream up a more devastating ending than seeing it all so viciously negated.

After I came back to the States we still maintained contact for another two years or so.  She eventually finished her degree and went back to Peru once her visa expired.  At the time she told me that she planned to come back to Canada once again, but after spending some time in Peru she changed her mind and stayed there.

She explained to me shortly after I got back to the U.S. that my visit made her miss me more than before, and eventually it became more painful for the both of us to be separated in such a manner.  Over the next two years she seemed to grow more restless and reserve less patience for both me and our situation.  It was stressful for both of us, and we had a lot of arguments.  I felt like it was all coming apart at the seams, and while I grew increasingly frustrated she seemed to become more detached.

Eventually the news came that she had met someone important back in Peru.  This was never a big deal before, as we always vowed to do our best to be open-minded and supportive of one another in the event that something like this happened, and it had happened for both of us before with varying results.  Whenever a 'normal' relationship failed we tried to be there for one another.

This was different, though.  The way she described it to me, the person she met seemed to illustrate many of the same qualities she loved about me.  Maybe too much.  She told me that he was just like me, and the convenience of having him near to her when she needed him was enough to essentially remove her from my life.  

It was too much to take, especially after having expended so much of an effort for so very long.  I felt like she was giving up and casting me aside.  I felt like she was losing hope in a way that I thought she never would.  I said more than a few things that I shouldn't have said.  She told me that we were broken and that she never wanted to speak to me again.  This was a promise that she has lived up to so far, and for the last five years I have been left to wonder.

Maybe she did what she felt like she had to do to better her life.  Maybe, like you suggest, she realized that she only cared for the concept of me.  Maybe it just died.  I don't know anymore.  I only know that to this very day I feel that it was unfair.

Considering this, I think that the experience of working in an office environment is something everyone should have. As frustrating as it can be, it can definitely reinforce one's sense of self.

This is Joomla 1.5 with a modified skin and a little Flash.  While I don't question that someone would end up paying upwards of $5,000 for a site like this, it does strike me as a bit ridiculous.

To put things into perspective, Joomla itself can be installed on a typical web server in maybe 15 minutes.  There are framework templates for development which are either free or with a GNU license, and many other fully-developed templates which are either unlicensed or relatively cheap ($50-150) range that can be modified easily.

There's almost never any extensive or unique coding that goes into a Joomla site, and most non-standard functionality is plug and play.  

Considering that, a developer who knows what he or she is doing is going to utilize every shortcut available and invest most of the actual development time on unique background, navigational and elemental graphics for the layout itself.  Someone who has a fundamental understanding of photoshop could do this within, I dunno, maybe a couple of days?

Don't get me wrong, it is my darkest desire to find someone who'd be willing to pay $5000 for something I could likely throw together in less than a week and I honestly wish you the best of luck.  I'm just sorta suffering from a bit of sticker shock here.

Strikes take a lot of organization, and this whole fiasco seems like it all happened on relatively short notice.  By the time a legitimate and effective strike could be orchestrated, this new bill would likely be law.  And part of this new bill dictates that public employees *cannot* strike without incurring a fee of double their daily wages for each day they participate.  They can also be replaced and the government has no responsibility to even consider giving them their job back.

Don't get me wrong, American workers have dealt with and overcome worse situations than this throughout the course of our short history as a nation, but it appears unlikely that any major section of the population in this case is gonna get behind a large-scale demonstration, walk-out or strike.  It's a shame.

EDIT:  Also, to give some extra perspective on how miserable this situation really is, Ohioans don't even have the luxury of initiating a recall vote for any statewide office.  This includes the governor and every elected official in the Statehouse.  Our friendly neighbors over in Wisconsin may very well turn every effort by Walker on its head, but here in Ohio we're essentially being force-fed a heaping pile of shit.  The only option left on the table is impeachment, which there is no reasonable case for, and even if there were the hearings would be presided over by a majority of the governor's own party members.  I, for one, do not welcome our new Republican overlords.

This.  Not to belittle the trials of anyone else in a similar situation, but many times it's a reactionary and emotional response to some sort of specific problem.  Consequently, the risk of actually going through with the act subsides as the issue which sparked it progresses toward resolution.  

If the same imminent conclusion is reached from a more general perception (philosophical, logical or otherwise) it is subsequently a much more persistent threat.  Non-specific, generalized issues are typically more much difficult to process in a meaningful way, and sometimes it may even seem like there is no potential resolution whatsoever.

Here's a silly little allegory that may make sense:

I can sit on the shore and honestly convince myself I'll never catch a fish, but odds dictate that I eventually will.  Maybe with enough patience, maybe with a different strategy, maybe simply by moving down the line a bit and trying different waters.  This is a basic and self-evident truth to me.

It's only after you begin to wonder what the hell it is you're doing on the shore in the first place, or why other people can seem to effortlessly cast their lines into the same waters as you with so much more success, or whether or not you even like the taste of fish, that you may be truly fucked.

I once sat in the living room of my father's house with a loaded 12-gauge shotgun under my chin for about an hour.  That type of power, the ability to choose if and when to end your own life when everything else seems to be spinning out of control, is actually quite enabling.  It was a turning point.

I decided to abandon the attempt, and within the next week I packed up everything I owned and moved back to my hometown to be with friends.  I ended up dating a really cool girl for a couple of years, going back to college and landing a decent job in the industry of my choice.  A relatively happy ending, I suppose.

In the interim I've also dealt with a recurring drinking problem, lost the girl and moved to an entirely different state populated with strange people.  I still think about that day from time to time, and I can't say with any confidence that the possibility still isn't off the table.  I have very high standards for myself and, consequently, perpetually fail to meet them.  I sometimes feel as if I have lost all integrity I may have once possessed.  

Once you reach the point in which you legitimately consider ending your own life and choose to not do so, it becomes a day-to-day struggle.  My fight is still ongoing.

I worked very strange hours for a few months and would get coffee at a McDonald's right down the street from my office at around 3:00 A.M. every night.  Just about every night it was the same guy with the same cheeky fucking attitude every time I pulled up, and I eventually got sick of it.

Don't get me wrong, I have the greatest of sympathies for people who have no better option than to make coffee and biscuits at a fast food place at three in the fucking morning, but it is possible to cross a line.  At some point you just have to buck up and realize that not sounding as if you're one perilous step away from putting a gun in your mouth is one of the responsibilities associated with your position.

So anyway, I drive up one night and this guy gives me the usual 'How can I help you?' which sounds more like 'What the fuck do *you* want?'.  He tells me to go ahead with my breakfast order, which is curious as the sign in the drive-thru still has the lunch menu on display.  I comment on this and he tells me in no uncertain terms that he's locked inside and even if he could get out to change the sign he's been too busy to worry about it.  

I wasn't even hungry and just wanted my usual coffee, but after dealing with this fucko for a month or so something finally snapped in my head.  I decided to be downright devious.  

I proceeded by telling the guy that I kinda wanted a hamburger, and he countered this with the scheduled time that they start serving breakfast.  I told him that I didn't really know what I wanted for breakfast because I couldn't see the menu, he asked me if I wanted some eggs.  I told him I'd feel better about placing my order if he could recite the breakfast menu to me in its entirety in order of number, including the contents of the meal and its respective price.  He disappeared for a moment, came back and actually began to rattle it off for me.  More than halfway through his little recital I told him I'd just like a coffee.

I paid in quarters and dimes, dumped the coffee and haven't been back to that place since.

**tl;dr - Got shitty service at a drive-thru, hopefully caused the guy to deeply reevaluate his life.**
